prof makes this class VERY easy to excel in. if you get anything below an A in this class you just simply put zero effort in

This class was on my back burner while I focused on 4 other classes, work, life, etc.

Prof. Froidevaux is a super sweet professor! I had her for both lab and lecture and she was great. Her lectures can be a little bit lengthy, but she thoroughly covers all the topics. The exams are not bad at all. 40 questions and if you review the study guide, you'll make a minimum B. The group project is lowkey tedious.. but not too terrible! :D
She is an excellent lecturer, she does take attendance but honestly her lectures are worth coming to. Take notes, review the study guide and you will pass.

analysis.name: Fatimah Jawad
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Super easy class and she's very nice. Just get work done and you're gonna pass attendance is not mandatory, I was barely in her class and still got an A, she responds to email so quickly, it was so amazing having her as a professor

Ms. Jawad is amazing—her class was so easy, and the work she gives out is mainly watching movies and answering questions about the art in the movie or art escape rooms. If you need to take any art/film class, I recommend you take her. Anything she teaches is an easy A.

Very fun professor. Took her for art appreciation and every lecture was engaging with kahoot (didn't use kahoot but something similar) style presentations. Discussions are due at the end of the day lecture day and a couple of "projects" throughout the course. Doing the homework and attending class will give you an easy A for sure.
Easy classes and lectures, you don't have to attend lectures but its helpful. Since you meet once a week, you have a lot of time to do the work.
She really cares about your projects, and she is helpful.

analysis.name: Raul Fernandez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 109 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Engineering Graphics is a very easy class but Fernandez is a bad professor. He prerecords his lectures (poorly) and makes you watch them at home, but in class he just rehashes the lecture without answering specific questions he asks us to ask him. The homework is due for all classes at the time of the first class, which is bad practice for a prof.

Not sure what to say. Everyone that I know is having to take this class again, including a majority of my class. The assignments and homework were easy, but it just doesn't seem to come together for the test. I have been doing engineering design for years yet decided to drop it. There is something is seriously wrong with this course.

i wish there is another prof. teachs intro to design. most of the students retaking this class. I do not like his teaching style and exams are not from book or video lectures . homeworks take a lots of time.

He's the only professor that teaches the class, so you're stuck with him. Goes with the flipped classroom model which works for some but for a lot, it makes it easy to put off the class until it's too late. Most of the video lectures are far too long due to his excessive talking. Wish I didn't have to take it again.

The class is fairly simple, but the way lectures are set up is ridiculous. He doesn't lecture, he posts videos online of his lectures and then answers any questions in class. So going to class is useless except that he does i clicker. Homework is easy if you have CAD experience, go to the lab, or watch videos. Also, the TA's usually have old notes

analysis.name: Dashiva Francois
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: When I first walked into his class, he told all of us to ignore his page on rate my professor because "those people have no idea what they are talking about." He cusses like a sailor, and has an obvious political agenda he pushes often, and I really feel like my input would be shut down from having a different perspective. He is childish for a prof
Incredibly unprofessional for a professor. He will talk down to you and completely disrespectful . I would not recommend this class to anyone and would definitely not take it again myself.

When you have a question or two about an assignment he will not help you. You can email him and talk to him however he will not help you, but instead try to refer you to the writing center instead of just giving you an answer. He is also not nice in his emails. To sum up, only pick him as your professor if you have no other choice.

Amazing professor, his lectures are all based around you and the questions you have. He doesn't take points off for late assignments and his grading is lenient, he encourages you to write in your own voice which made this class very fun. I was worried going into this class because of all the bad reviews but he was lovely and his class was very fun.

He is a good teacher overall and I probably would take this class again. But grading takes awhile. Kindve hard to reach outside class. But his lectures were fun and informative. The syllabus and rubrics were iffy.

analysis.name: Noelle Fields
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fields is great. She provides accurate lecture materials, timely grading, movie quizzes (some multiple choice), a light workload, and excellent feedback. Heads up, she requires her students to participate in a "Convergence Day", but it was an amazing learning experience and you'll get to interact with students from other professions.

Dr. Fields is an excellent professor! After enjoying a prior course with her, I took her Direct Practice of Aging class. The workload includes weekly discussions, quizzes, and a major paper at the end, with Convergence Day required. Her grading is fair but may take time. Highly recommend her!

Dr. Fields is an exceptional professor. She grades promptly, provides helpful feedback, and shares engaging articles and videos. Additionally, she offers extra credit and is not a harsh grader. The quizzes are open-book and straightforward. I highly recommend her and plan to take another course with her.

MSW Fall 24 - Excellent professor! She is accessible, provides great feedback and caring. Her assignments are entertaining. I believe I signed up for another class she teaches for Spring 25.I wish all professors were like her.
I REALLY enjoyed Dr. Fields. She was passionate and cared about her class. She was very relatable and easy to talk to. If I could have her for another class I would take it 100%

analysis.name: Farah Naz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was very nice and gave extra credit opportunities. I got a bad grade on the final but still got an A bc of how nice her grading system is. This is a class you can kinda forget about and focus on other stuff but not completely. It's still math and a decent amount of stuff to memorize and work at. Dr. Naz was very flexible and forgiving
This professor was phenomenal, she had amazing lectures and the HW was not draining. 2 midterm exams and 1 final exam. Labs are fun, and the lab reports after are not bad.
Her class is good overall. Just make sure you stay on top of the homework, carefully study the test reviews, and don't underestimate the quiz. If you keep up with those, you'll be fine in the class.
Overall an average class. I could've gotten a better grade if I tried more. As long as you study and pay attention you will do well.

analysis.name: Tyler Garner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Assignments can't be done in advance, but are every week instead. You are basically exercising and eating appropriately, using plans you will design yourself. It's up to you to actually do them. You do learn things about weight/muscle management, though, and can interact with others on the discussion board. No tests at all, just weekly updates.

Tyler D. Garner was a great professor. The class had three exams and a final, and he drops the lowest exam grade, which helped a lot. There were some writing assignments, but he explained them clearly and was always willing to help. His in-class exam reviews closely matched the exams. He's very nice and jokes with students.

Dr. Garner himself was great. He gave lots of extensions if you needed and always answered his emails very quick. But if you think this class is an easy A, it is not. There are multiple quizzes and exams up to 150 questions. There is no partial credit which is verryyy frustrating, so make sure you read your textbook and start on assignments early!

Mr. Garner is that professor we all hope for. He took time to help me out when I was confused over a topic and didn't seem bothered by me stopping by his office. I would take him again and do yourself a favor, you will not think twice about dropping this one.
Great teacher who cares about his students. Workload wasn't bad. You show up and do the assignments, pass easily.

analysis.name: George Rice
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The homework stipulations become INSANE once you get to GUI's but he really knows his stuff and has great sense of humor. Really easy to talk to but the homework will totally test your "Am I cut out for this?" OOP class was probably the most realistic and practical class I've taken for Comp Science. Not out to fail you but don't expect to cruise.

I forgot to leave a rating when I had him last semester and I heard he's no longer teaching at UTA, so I'm just leaving this here to show my appreciation to him if he ever reads this or if he ever comes back to teaching at UTA or anywhere else. Please take him for any course you can if you ever get the chance. He's incredible.

Teacher is A+, but the amount of homework is truly obscene. I almost hesitate to say it because the University should focus more on this kind of work rather than inane, irrelevant garbage that they like to teach in other classes. For whatever it's worth, my ability to program improved. Every other class I took suffered.

I love George Rice. His lectures and slides are VERY good. He does pop quizzes for attendance but always tries to give us the answer before hand. Coding homeworks each week that usually have extra cred points and will always answer our emails no matter the time if possible. Great professor, will miss him since its his last semester. Genuinely kind.

Professor Rice is one of the greatest CS professors at UTA. Pop quizzes is an attendance grade and post lecture quizzes are infinite attempts. Homework's are hard and test reviews are similar to exams. Do all of the test reviews and you will succeed. I was clueless the first couple weeks but you learn quickly. Fast paced course but great proffesor.

analysis.name: Gyde Martin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: overall wasn't a hard class (like AP lang) There were only three grades (papers) in the class, first 2 essays got a 90/100 plus tons of feedback. third essay got a lot more help from prof and writing center. got the worst grade (90/120 75%) and her only note was to change how I introduced authors. nice but lectures too long and erratic grading.

She is a very nice and caring professor, but when it comes to be time for essays or even grading them she wouldn't really specify what was wrong with it. When asking a question she will answer about unnecessary things and not the question itself.

Juts avoid this class if possible.She knows her stuff but you will be in total dark for the paper & annotated bibliography total %40 of your grade. There will be quizzes every day and she'll ask real details such as what kind of horse a minor character was riding on.She is sweet and will treat you with respect but if you want to pass dont take her

Loved Dr. Martin's Children's Lit class! Read every time, there will be quizzes. Pay attention in class and take good notes, you'll need them to study for the test. She is pretty straight forward about her projects, gives you options to pick which one best suits your major's focus. Would for sure take her again if I could!

This is truly one of the worst professor that i've had.  She take attendance,it is 20% to your grade. Whenever you ask her something about the assignment she'll said go back to the book. Absolutely horrible,never take her if you have another option.Sometimes she just keep talking in class and you don't even know what she's talking about.

analysis.name: Genevieve Godfrey
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This professor was nice. She reads off the slides in class and also records it on Echo360. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures. Exams are taken in class with lockdown/webcam. Extra credit is given at the end of the semester. There are 4 exams, 3 practice exams, and weekly quizzes. Lowest gets dropped. Overall not a bad class!

I would absolutely take this professor again without hesitation. The course is memory-based and can be difficult, but she makes it as easy as possible. She gives helpful tips and examples, truly cares about her students, and is very understanding that life happens sometimes and can conflict with due dates.

Took for Anatomy and Physiology I, had exams every 2 weeks. Lectures moved very fast. Professor also cancelled class pretty often, and while she did do meetings online, it was still a little hard to catch up sometimes. Overall, it was an average class.
Mostly reads off slides, and gives not very useful information thats on the slides. Her slides give examples that you don't need to know. She doesn't respond to emails quickly, takes her weeks.

analysis.name: leigh griffis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It really isn't fair to rate this professor when there is a coach who is the one grading assignments. There are outlines for every assignment that breaks down exactly what should be in every section of your paper. As long as you follow the format of the example papers and the rubric there should not be an issue getting an A.
Be aware there is no leniency with this individual. Under no circumstances that are out of your control, will she work with you. Takes her job way too seriously for an online class. Get a life.

all modules are PPT no lecture. 3 easy exams. For DB & paper, she is a strict grader. Be very thorough, start early, write center abide by rubric & sample paper. TurnItIn below 30% no resubmissions. She does not have a problem giving F grades so be very aware. It takes a lot of time to find/read thru all the articles needed so start early.

The instructor does not interact with the online class. There is a syllabus that you follow and some of the instructions can be interpreted in a different way. Be careful, she grades tough. 
Not a very good course on a graduate level. Very disappointed after working so hard and paying for the course out of pocket.

The professor is not present but this is because coaches are the first point of contact. I made an almost perfect 100% after being out of school for 5 years. Anyone here complaining is upset because they want to be spoon fed information, at the graduate level you should be able to at least comprehend simple directions and rubrics.

analysis.name: Gabriela Rodriguez

The lab is just a waste of time

She's one of those professors who you believe is going to be one of the greatest professors you'll ever have but ends up disappointing you. 3 written assignments, a group project, and 3 exams. She's kind and understanding of personal circumstances. Extremely picky grader, little to no feedback, and doesn't grade based on the rubric. Reads off the slides and often contradicts the lecture professor. She discouraged us from reaching out during the first exam because she was traveling, which felt unprofessional. Wouldn't recommend her lab.

be prepared to not understand what your grade in the course is. Grading takes forever and feedback is vague. I will say that she does seem to genuinely care about her students. She tried her best to learn everyone's names. If you actually want to understand what is going on in the class, take a different professor for the lab portion

I'm writing this on new year's day because I hope you don't ruin your year. Dont start the year with Professor Rodriguez. Also she tends to wait until the last minute to grade stuff. Had me watching my grade on thanksgiving rather than spending time with my family

analysis.name: Jeremy Glass
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Glass  other 2425 professors. Young, fun, and smart man. He has printable fill in notes that help organize the sections into easy test studying materialreferences. It may seem as if he works through his lecture fast sometimes, it is only because he is trying to cover each and every variation that could appear on the test. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

He is a very helpful person, who wants you to succeed in his class and other classes. A true gentleman and a scholar. Truly cares about his students. Easy class if you fill out the notes and pay attention.

HE WAS AWESOME. You can miss class some and be fine because he reviews the class before the actual test. You get to use a 3X5 note card ON THE TEST. You get one retest which is almost the exact same as the original test. If you take his class you will not regret it. Math is/always has been hard for me, but he made a lot of sense. I would take again
Very easy class to take online. There is no way you can fail. His homework is incredibly easy and I managed to get a 100 on every test including the final. He is very helpful.

AWESOME. He taught so well, MyMathLab has all assignments and attendance to lecture is taken and bonus points awarded for it, so GO TO CLASS. Hours in the lab are logged and you must have a minimum of 30 per semester in the lab. Would take him again. He's very accessible and cares.

analysis.name: Marcus Hendershot
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very easy class, should be impossible to fail as long as you turn in assignments and quizzes, which are all open note. Records all lectures and posts slides in canvas, also does Microsoft Teams meetings to take essentially as an online course. Very flexible with due dates, allowed me to turn in a quiz for full points even after 3 days past due.

Amazing lectures. If you go to class and are decent at using your resources you'll get an A. I didn't do either for the first half of the semester, had to study a lot for the last exam (which isn't comprehensive), got a near perfect score and got an A. Take him but don't slack off since each grade is worth so much. He records his lectures.

If you somehow do bad in this class, that is entirely your fault. Mr. Hendershot had engaging lectures, that he was clearly passionate about. And you actually learn a thing or two that you could actively apply in real life, whether it be conversation or action. His papers are simple as long as you can write one like an adult and the tests are free.

Lectures are interesting. All slides shown in class can be found on Canvas along with recordings of his lectures. Mainly just 3 exams with some light assignments. Easy class that you can learn something interesting or important depending how you view political science.

The professor is good. His grading, however is only based on one essay, few quizzes and exams. You dont have to go to lectures. Just go through the slides for exams. Make sure to do good on that one essay though. Overall, a pretty easy A class.

analysis.name: Shaun House
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE DR. HOUSE!!! Such a kind and respectruly person! We read a 10 page article each week and talk about it in class! As long as you make an effort, show to class and actually participate, you will not only get the grade you want, but you'll have a blast in his class! The class discussions were a lot of fun and he ends class really early!

One of my Fave profs at UTA. He's so cool and chill. When he lectures it's more of a conversation with the class  and he relates current issues with Philosophy. All the exams are essay but it's super easy if you come to class and read the book. I recorded his lectures too. Final was take-home.

A lot of students will say this class is an easy A, if you take this course seriously like any other core course. The assignments were lengthy but they were interesting to do and I learned a lot. Lectures were truly great. You will truly learn a lot and it will open your mind to topics you will remember forever and apply to your actual life.

Great professor who truly cares for his students, and all his assignments are graded based on completion. Attendance is necessary however, he gives you plenty of time to finish assignments and often cancels class to give you that time back. Most weeks, you would only have to go to class once. Truly inspirational and attentive to his students!

This is an easy A class. 25% for attendance and 25% for class participation. Two easy papers worth 50%. The professor is great and easy to talk to. The class is just about discussing morality. Not much is required to do in class except for thinking. The papers are also graded leniently. You will enjoy the class and broaden your perspective.

analysis.name: Scott Hilton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Love Professor Hilton! As someone who knew nothing about photography, he made sure I fully understood everything. Get ready to spend a LOT of money on this class though. Film and Paper are $$$. He does a great job of giving feedback when printing. He'll tell you what you need to do to get a quality print. You ask for help, he's immediately there!

My main issues with the class was I had to work outside of class a LOT for this class, and it was also real expensive. I don't really have a problem with Scott though, he helped me learn a lot, he's pretty funny, played ukulele.

Best photo professor/teacher! He knows what to teach, he gives you all you need include feedback on your photo works. Participation matters, but not really. If you do your project as directed, you will get an A.

He's a decent guy. 6-7 photography assignments (some are introductory, later ones are more complicated) with 4-8 photos each. Uses Lightroom CC for editing. 1 research/ presenting project over a photographer. You'll have to buy paper ($20), ink ($26), and a portfolio ($19). Phone cameras/ DSLR are acceptable for his course.
Scott is awesome. Knows everything about alt photo.

analysis.name: Halen Watkins
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is literally the best professor I have ever had. He is very clear with his grading and is very understanding. His grades are mostly lecture based quizzes which weight the most and about 30% is a book review that is a pretty fast read. The lecture is on echo360 if you happen to miss class for some reason. I would 10/10 would take him again.

Lwk the goat, took his class Fall 2024 and his lectures were always interesting. He says he is in his "mean girl era" due to people taking his class for granted, but if you just do the work you should be fine. I'm not sure if he still does this but he doesn't do lectures on Fridays, so if yall want a great history teacher, hes the guy.

Dr. Watkins is a great professor to take! Although his lectures are not posted on a slideshow or online modules, he discusses everything that will be on the Midterm and Final Exam. He has a clear grading rubric where he provides feedback on assignments. Coming from a third year student, Dr. Watkins has been the best professor I have had so far!

Class isn't difficult if you show up and listen/take notes during lecture. Entire class is based off lectures that Dr. Watkins freestyles. He is extremely knowledgable and seems very genuine. However, he likes respect and doesn't want kids coming in late or making a bunch of noise during the lecture. No homework other than the book you have to read

I was intimidated at first for this course because I am not the best in history, but Watkins was extremely straightforward. 8 quizzes (10 questions, no time limit, open note and taken once) with 2 Exams(essays, open note, no time limit) and 2 Books reports which were actually interesting books. All the info is on his PowerPoints. Also 1presentation

analysis.name: Heather Arterburn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would NOT recommend for A & P II. HW is weekly & timed (15 minutes). No grade drops or curves. No extra credit. Opens a few past homework assignments to re-do, but if you get a 100 on those, then re-doing does not help. 3 lecture exams, 2 practicals with photos you have not seen before, & 1 final. Holds grades until she feels like releasing them.

I thought it was a pretty straightforward class, everything you need to know to prepare for the 4 exams (and the optional final) is on her slides. She sometimes gives hints about exam questions during lecture, worth going. She is very strict about pre-labs tho so if you have her section don't be late! She won't accept them after lab starts.

I too don't get the hate. Professor Arterburn was great. She used lots of lectures, which could take time to get through, but they were well done and informative. The homework was fairly graded with a good rubric (usually). You get multiple attempts on all the quizzes and and lab assignments, and the tests are directly from the quizzes.

This was the least helpful professor I have ever had. She not only was never helpful but the material put out was not helpful either. For "homework" they were timed quizzes that you have one attempt at. When asking to review exams, she refuses and quotes that in the "real world" you will need to know this stuff by heart (ie spelling). overall sucks

I took this class because it was a prerequisite, but never again. Once I figured I could take ecology or zoology instead, my college life changed for the better. Her lectures are boring and not inclusive. She basically only relies on exam grades because the few homework assignments she provides are not helpful towards the overall grade at all.

analysis.name: Ida Klang
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 66 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Take her!!! Professor Klang knows what she teaches and knows how to teach it well. She knows how to simplify tricky concepts in order for students to understand. As for the course work its easy. There is one homework assignment for each module which just consist of 15-20 questions. Other than that she provides review days for most of the test.

Dr. Klang is very passionate and caring about biology. You can tell she cares about her students and tries to help them as much as possible. 1-2 HWs per week. 4 Tests and 4 practice tests per semester. She allows 2 attempts on practice tests. 2-3 chapters on each test. This class does have a final. She's funny, very nice, and engaging in lectures.

Knew a good bit of biology prior to this class, but Dr. Klang really expanded on that and made it fun. She makes dull slides entertaining and gives good ways to memorize concepts. Additionally, she goes out of her way to link videos and create reviews prior to each Midterm Exam. Very caring and loved being in her class!

Had this professor in my first semester of college and just have to write a review. The best professor at UTA! I struggled with Biology ever since I was a kid, and she made it so easy to understand. The only professor I've had that is understanding of LDB technical difficulties, which eased my testing anxiety.

She is super helpful, has many resources for studying, encourages interaction amongst students and encouraged us to help each other. HWs are great for studying material and lectures are always more than reading off the slides.

analysis.name: Isabel Zaera
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing Professor, there is a lot of homework, but it is all online and shouldn't take more than about 30 minutes to complete. Be prepared for the final exams; there is a test portion and a speaking portion. She is super sweet and caring and is very lenient. All you have to do is communicate with her, and she answers pretty fast.

The syllabus looks scary, but it's paced well. Every week or so is a new chapter and she has you do speaking activities, connect assignments, and a writing assignment. She's very helpful and will answer any questions you have whether it's in or out of class. There's only two big tests and she gives you extra credit opportunities. Great professor!

I hadn't taken Spanish since elementary school and was dreading this class. She made the material so accessible and genuinely cared about our understanding before moving on. She was constantly letting us know what kind of questions we would be tested on and making sure we understood exactly what would be expected of us. Would 100% take her again.

Really sweet prof who truly wishes to help you learn Spanish. She has us do speaking activities during class which can be daunting but are seriously not that bad, actually rather helpful for getting used to speaking the language. 1442 was def more challenging than 1441 but with Prof Zaera I struggled far less than I know I would've otherwise.

Her syllabus looks so scary but trust she opens up past due assignments near exams so we can 'practice' and also work up to a 100% and also gives out extra credit. Attendance is mandatory and if you're there 80% of the time she drops the final for you

analysis.name: Heather Charles
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 125 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: For the first time in my three years at UTA I've scored a B with this professor. I've gotten A's in all my sciences including patho, this professor is probably one of, if not the worst I've taken. Save yourself and take this, what should've been an easy A class, with Ida Klang, if you can! Honorlock is the worst, literally no need for two cameras.

She is probably one of the best professors I've taken. In any of her classes, all you need to do to get a good grade is show up and pay attention. Her lectures cover almost, if not all, test material and she is always looking for questions. I've taken her for multiple classes and it's the same in all. She is a fantastic professor.

As long as you complete the quizzes, study intricately the lectures weather on echo 360 or in person (highly recommend not missing the lectures) and completing the learning goals and depth it will be impossible to fail. There is no textbook for the class, but that may change in the near future since she is currently writing one.

I was forced to take this professor as there were no other options available. Terrible experience. Exams are lockdown browser + extra side camera. There's no reason this class should have 2 cameras during exams, it should have been an easy A. The exams are also nothing like the slides!!! She doesn't give extra credit. Do not take her.

This is my second time having this professor. (A&P II & now Nutrition). Every class is the same format: Do the homework + study the powerpoint and you will get an A. She will never test you on something that isn't on those slides.The side camera for nutrition online is a downside, but I've had no issues with it!

analysis.name: Tom Ingram
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

Unclear rubrics, irrelevant coursework, and inadequate feedback on why unnecessary points were deducted. I have had the same experience as other reviewers. AVOID IF YOU CAN!!

I don't usually write reviews on my professors, but I did feel the need to warn future students. She is an EXTREMELY picky grader and I agree with previous reviews that she deducts points like crazy and you shouldn't waste your time asking her about your grade. I would have definitely chosen Dombrowsky over her.

Super nice and chill! You have to be on time and attendance matters but the class is pretty easy overall. analysis.name: Yuan Peng

PENG IS THE MAN! This is man is one of the best the university has to offer. If you take it get ready to work!

analysis.name: Paula Wyman

amazing professor. I recommend downloading the powerpoints before class and writing your notes while she teaches. Look at student success videos & blueprints before every exam! Dr. Ravenscraft is one of the BEST professors in the department! Her lectures are very clear and easy to understand. She's ALWAYS willing to answer questions and is flexible w/ due dates. Grading for essays are easy but you'll have to put a little bit of effort if you want an A in the class. Participation is a must. Overall great experience.

Great teacher! Explains all assignments thoroughly and provides all necessary information in order to make A's on your assignments. Everything is very straight forward. Participation grades count a lot in her class. She is immature, insults you in front of class if you do come prepared. She was helping, but I did not like the way she taught, I felt her class more like a discussion class and group work. Attendance is mandatory!

Good teacher.. Not a hard class but a lot of work and reading assignments.. She helped make my writing skills improve.. I would recommend her if you like to write, but also if u want a teacher who will be straight up with u help u when u need it.

This professor is horrible. He teaches much more than what is necessary for PHYS 1443, his exams have nothing to do with the sample exams he provides on blackboard. Make sure you do all the homework and get a good grade on the lab because you'll really need that. Do not take him.

The class consisted of 10 hw assignments, 3 midterms, 1 cumulative final all through ExpertTA. Would take him again!

Dr White was one of the easiest classes ever. I took online PHYS 1441 and all of the tests and homework were open book with no lockdown browser. analysis.name: Angela Garner

Overall, this professor was really good, and the class was easy to follow. It does require plenty of reading, studying, and online meetings with peers and coaches, but everything is clear and manageable. I'd definitely take this course again.

Awesome prof! Super funny, made each class enjoyable, and created a communicative and fun environment. Great at teaching content, and the online textbook (while annoying to navigate) is helpful and easy to get good grades with. Extremely respectful; had no problems letting me use my preferred pronouns for the very gendered language.

She's a really nice professor, she let me take the midterm early bc of a funeral, no questions asked. Content is also really easy, homework you can attempt over and over for a 100 and she prepares you really well for tests (spent two weeks in class reviewing for the midterm). Also gives extra credit opportunities to add to your test scores.

Professor Gkergki's lectures are incredible, and she is very understanding about students' circumstances if they are not able to attend class consistently. Would 100% take one of her courses again!

Antonia Gkergki is great, and I only got a C in her class because I am lazy and do not care about econ, but for those who try just a little will succeed i would take this class again. She is nice and easy-going
Professor Gkergki was really great and it is honestly difficult to fail her class. Just do the one homework assigned that week, and show up sometimes.

I love this professor so much, I wish I can take her again next semester :( If you read up on the material before class and watch the videos she provides with the notes, it's so easy to pass this class. Rudest and most arrogant human beings I have ever had the displeasure of meeting. Awful is an understatement. Very Difficult at the beginning, more difficult at the end. Intentionally he makes things complicated, so the students will say he is tough. long time you need to spend on HW which they are not related to what he "reads" from his VAGUE notes. I DON'T RECOMMEND HIM TO ANY BODY.

The professor speaks in a thick accent and mumbles/goes off topic ALOT. He will expect you to already know Python for this intro class. analysis.name: Brandi Andrade

I love brandi! She's is so fun and her assignments are super easy! She's spunky, and knows how to make you enjoy a 3 hour lecture.  also, her outfits are cute

She is a good lecturer, very energetic. However, she is not a nice person. Two straight forward exams and a paper that you HAVE to go see spending your own money and tickets ain't cheap!! She is the toughest grading professor I ever had. Week after week its multiple assignments that are long and even after I have put in hours to do the assignments she doesnt grade off effort at all. Well, when she gives her lectures, she seems alright. If you need to talk to her about something, forget it. She's extremely rude and accused me of cheating with no evidence whatsoever! analysis.name: De An Roper
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Roper is so kind and willing to work with students. She does require a lot of article reading, but they are interesting. I would definitely take her class again if I could.

Professor Roper is a fantastic professor. She's highly accessible outside class, eager to help students learn, & will hold extra Teams sessions & discussions to help students with assignments. A difficult class, but Dr. Roper is amazing.  She has high standards/expectations, but is very clear and fair about them. Overall, an amazing professor- just teaches an intense course.

I had her for SOCW 2238 Intro to Substance Use Disorders. She was a great professor with good communication and feedback. She has one major book report assignment that she informs you about at the beginning of the semester. Easy grader.

Dr. Roper is a genuine professor trying to teach one of the most difficult classes in SW. She cares greatly about your understanding. Papers are difficult but she helps a lot!

analysis.name: Amy Bernhard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Such a fun class, definitely recommend. Make sure to do the readings every week, but the textbook is actually really interesting. It's not hard to get a 100, just submit on time.

Amy is one of the best professors I've had at UTA. Her Creative Writing class helped me grow SO much as a writer and as a person. The professor gives zeroes on assignments if you use AI.

Can't miss more than 8 days or she'll lower by 1 letter grade. She had a midterm, final & a 4-5 pg essay due at the end. She's really nice & caring. Easy class.

Amy (She has us call her Amy) is a great professor! She gives great lecture and provides lots of great reading material. There's a lot of writing but mostly short one page writing due once a week analyzing works read outside class. She calls on class a lot for answers, so be ready for that. Great professor and great person.

Teacher was very laid back and pretty caring when it came to class.While she makes class enjoyable, being present is a must as there is a major group project for this class.

I really liked this class! She was fun and kept lectures light & easy to follow while making sure we learned all we needed to succeed. I think most of her bad reviews are from her first years of teaching so she's gotten much better in my opinion!

The class has very little to no homework

He is caring and understanding. You will surely enjoy his class despite being a bit tough grader! Quality matters, friends!

The professor was amazing. He would mostly focus on assignments. Sometimes he'd share something that did not relate to the course. He'd bring humor into class. But he is a strict grader. It doesn't mean he takes off points from tasks. He also gives chances to revise our work.

analysis.name: Enid Arvidson

I definitely recommend.

Excellent lectures. Good discussion. Interesting c

Discussion posts weekly, later requiring video responses.

Took Latina experience with her and it was a very easy class. 4 discussion boards, 2 papers and a group project. She is also a easy grader just do the assignments and you'll pass with an easy A.

Karla is great she is not strict she considers her students  "adults" so if you read or come to class is up to you  it will reflect the grade. she has lots of experience teaches information from the book and translates it into real scenarios to better understand the concept. analysis.name: Ashish Sedai

review_highlights.comment: smart guy, however, with this intelligence comes a lot of arrogance. kind of stuck up and rude at times, especially towards women. overall, rude but good at teaching and organizing his class.

He's a very understanding professor and genuinely cares about you and your grades. Dr. Sedai is an excellent teacher and knows the content of his class very well.  He is a pleasant and approachable person.

analysis.name: Ashley Hall

She's very  calming personality and is very relatable which also makes her a pretty cool professor! I love how she provides a vast amount of examples that are relatable to you. analysis.name: Jonathan Asaadi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Professor Asaadi is great. It's easy to be lazy in his class since this grading system is so chill. Having said that, be as active as possible. The only people in the class are people who don't apply themselves very well, which sometimes frustrates Asaadi. He loves try-hards, and he might even bump you are grade if you really show him you're trying.

Dr. Assadi is AMAZING!! However his take home tests are NOT a joke. And his final is EVEN WORSE, even though it's all open note. Show up to class and really understand his lectures!! They are crucial to you success in the class! I didn't go to class often so I payed the consequences!

Dr. Asaadi is a great teacher! I did have a few problems in his class, for instance, he would go super fast and it would be hard to keep up with him. His take home test in my opinion were very difficult unreasonably and have a lot of parts to it that are very confusing. You would find an answer you think is right but then have more to find! Hard!

It was Dr. Asaadi's first time teaching PHYS 3313, but he did a great job. All potential exam questions are provided ~2 classes in advance, and he will pick out questions to be on the exams. This class's concepts are challenging, but getting a good grade is easy with the way he structured it. Put in the time and come to class, and you'll be okay.

Really enjoyed professor Assadi's class! He is really good at explaining difficult concepts and is really easy to understand! He gives 2 take home tests (15% each) which are pretty difficult, HW due at end of semester  (15%), labs (10%), 15% attendance quizzes (which are not hard) and 30% final in which you can use ANY resources but very very hard!

analysis.name: Ashraf Warda
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I can't say enough about Professor Warda. She's a tremendous professor and will help you if you put in the work. Attendance is not required and lecture is recorded. Study hard for the 2 exams the 2nd one is harder than the 1st. She gives out "bonus points" in class if you participate. Lastly, she gives a TON of partial credit on exams. Take Her!

Dr Warda explains concepts for statics very well and even makes time during the lecture and at the end for you to ask questions if anything was confusing. Study extra hard for the second midterm, it is more difficult than the first and will primarily cover the latter chapters despite the exam covering about 4-5 chapters. Don't skip out on the hw!!

Dr. Ashraf is an amazing professor. She's very generous with her extra credit as long as you participate in class. The homeworks are pretty tough but they give you plenty of preparation for the exams. Same thing with the reviews she provided. Sad she doesn't teach other courses in CE.

Professor Warda was one of the best I ever had! She set the standard really high. She was able to break down complex statics concepts into simpler forms and really helped me, a student that usually struggles with math, grasp the subject. She would work through numerous example problems in lecture that greatly help! Many bonus points on tests!!!

Although not mandatory, attendance and note taking is very important. Offers many chances for extra credit. Lectures are thorough and concise with great examples. The book is not needed. Offers partial credit on all assignments and exams. Very accessible outside of class with quick email responses. Late sometimes but it doesn't affect learning.

analysis.name: Ashley Lemke
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Lemke is very young, outgoing, and pretty great overall. Her classes are interesting and she does her best to engage students by doing activities a d having class discussions. Random attendance checks will get you extra credit. Tests are extremely easy. If you want to learn and have fun take her classes.

Dr. Lemke is awesome. She cares about her field and it shows. I loved how she let her class mold where topics took us with every chapter on different archaeology discoveries. Graded on 2 tests/2 papers/ and participation. She was always approachable and loved to engage with answering our questions. Take her!

Dr. Lemkey is a great professor! She's very outgoing, laid back, and you can tell she loves teaching. She talks very fast but it is mostly just examples to help you understand the concepts in the course better. I would not skip class because there are a few in-class assignments, but if you do, she is very understanding.

I love her so much, she was the one that intrigued me to study Archaeology.  There is only two essays and two tests, including the final. Very lenient grader, and very helpful through emails. It was a pleasure coming to her class every day, she made the topics she covered interesting!

Sad that she's leaving UTA. To her next uni and students: you're in for a treat. Dr. Lemke is spectacular, and her lectures are always engaging. She's understanding and caring and does not grade harshly. If you have an interest in archaeology, you can always come talk to her. Reminds me of Ms. Stacy from Anne with an E, if you've seen that show.

analysis.name: Ashley Johnson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took 1301 during the summer and she was really sweet and definitely makes you a better writer. She gives great feedback! Ms. Johnson is very willing to help you if you just ask. Very committed. However, she hands out few As and almost no 100s for essays. If you are looking for an easy A, this is not the class unless you are a natural writer.

I took Ms. Johnson's class over the summer and she was great. Provided lots of resources including sample essays to help us, reviewed our first drafts, and provided detailed feedback on how to revise. She doesn't give 100s on essays though, and grades pretty strictly, so make sure to read the prompt/rubric. Final grade heavily depends on 3 essays.

At first, I didn't do so well in her class but she was very helpful in giving me feedback for each of my papers and helped me achieve the grade I wanted by giving me extra credit opportunities and by reviewing my papers to see if I was on the right track. Not every English teacher puts this much effort into their students, she's the best.

I took Ms. Johnson's British Lit class and I absolutely loved it. She is an amazing teacher who provides a great class for her students. She is engaging and I looked forward to every single class. As long as you do what she asks of you and read the lit she provides, you'll be golden! My favorite professor I've had.

Ms. Johnson was a great teacher, she doesn't talk to you, she talks with you. She is caring and very good about her feedback on your paper. However, you should expect to have some heavy grading, she gives A's a bit more rarely. If you take her feedback well and fix your mistakes you can expect B's and A's.

analysis.name: Ashley Palmer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Palmer is AMAZING! I learned so much from her class and her lectures are not boring. She is so cooperative and caring especially during unprecedented times like these. Her feedback is really helpful and she is all about improvement. Course load is average but includes a lot of self reflection. Overall I highly recommend her for any class!

Dr. Palmer is the best professor Ive ever had! Her lectures were very engaging and she always incorporated relevant topics that we are experiencing today. It is clear that she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed not only in school but in life. Ive learned so much from Dr. Palmer and would recommend her to everyone.

My favorite professory I've ever had. She is so caring and compassionate. She acknowledges that life is so much more than school and she does everything she can to help you succeed. I am so sad I won't have her for another course because she really changed my academic perspective. She's incredible.

analysis.name: Christopher Atkins

Very chill dude. For an intro-level course, his class lifted some weight off my already heavy workload. As long as you already know how to write essays and cite sources correctly, you will easily get an A.
He was really cool and chill throughout the semester and very understanding. He is lenient with late submissions and is always willing to work with you. Take him if you can!

analysis.name: Ashley Guy

Great lecturer. Definitely recommend taking him for any course. Made one of the most dreaded courses in the program enjoyable. His assignments are difficult, but he's fair and loves to give out partial credit. Attend lecture and put effort into the homework and you'll be prepared for exams.

Hes a great lecturer, actually teacher very well and cares about the students learning the material. Some homework is tough, but he is always willing to help. Attendance isnt necessary but dont miss lecture. Grades very fair, partial credit.

I am not happy with professor guy. This semester has been very hard on students with the pandemic and the winter storm halting classes for a week. She is an amazing teacher and loves her students and her job. probably too much too much, you'll see what i mean... you must take her for the internship class! easy A, easy upper level hours, you don't even have a class to attend but 2-3 times, and she will do anything she can to help out.

Easily the best teacher in the department, and may be the only one soon, as the dean is trying to run off all the faculty. She is extremely helpful, will stay after class or meet elsewhere to help you. Very understanding and wants to see her students excel.

analysis.name: Raymond Atta-Fynn

analysis.name: Austin Allen

Amazing professor, His lectures are interesting, group assignments are easy. Easy grader and overall enjoys teaching his students

analysis.name: Amy Austin

review_highlights.comment: Dra. Austin is a great professor. She is very straightforward and the syllabus tells you exactly what you need to do. Easy A if you do all the work and follow her feedback.

Dr. Austin is a great professor! I really enjoyed her class. The tests aren't hard. There are a few essays, but they aren't too bad. It's really important to do the reading before every class. Class is pretty much discussion of the reading. Spanish Lit with her is not scary/intimidating, she makes it very accessible to students.

Dr. Austin is very enthusiastic about Spanish and Spain.  She is also very understanding and caring towards students. One big project (no exams) to be created in the FabLab about some aspect of Spain.  Lots of reading and analyses to be done, but all very thought provoking.  It does take considerable effort, but it is a interesting and fun class.

Dr. Austin is friendly and caring, but she won't coddle you, either. There is lots of reading and class participation/group work, and a few challenging projects, but overall the class is work taking. The midterms and final are personal interviews conducted entirely in Spanish.

ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AT UTA.  She is extremely passionate, as well as lenient and understanding.  I truly feel that she was able to teach something to every single one of her students.  Can't wait to have her again!

analysis.name: Erin Austin

she was so careless passionless and racist and would make the lectures about her “bad days” that were just regular inconveniences to her giant class of very diverse students. i definitely do not recommend taking her if you want to learn but if you want to scrape by with the bare minimum sure. she is proof sequence classes need more options.

analysis.name: Austin Loignon

One of the most amazing History professors at UTA. He really cares for his students and loves when they reach out. Loignon is a great professor and he and the TA are kind and funny and give good feedback. The assignments are mostly bi-weekly writing assignments about what was discussed in lectures the past two weeks. If you take good notes it's pretty easy to write one out in about an hour. The final and mid-term were also essays and the grading was lenient.

analysis.name: Aubrey Rhoden

He tends to talk a lot about the Republican party and was upset that Obama was reelected. Can be rude at times, depending on how well we get along.

analysis.name: Jose Ayala-Rodríguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

It's helpful to read the textbook before a class, but he does go over a PowerPoint that summarizes each chapter so it's fine to not read as long as you take notes here (I didn't read the textbook).

Very nice, young professor who seems to really care and value his students. He's very approachable. Speaking/emailing him outside of class was super easy. His quizzes are worded a little confusing sometimes, but if you read the book you will be good. Tests are SUPER easy. He relies on the book a lot for his assignments, so just go to class and read

Do well on quizzes and you'll be fine. Answers are shown afterwards. The Midterms/Finals are literally the quiz questions/answers. Even though participation is an element of your grade, I only talked once for the entire semester and still got an A. To be on the safe side, just talk a few times. Other than that, he is a great and caring professor

most of what we had were quizzes along with a paper, we also had a midterm and a final that were based on the quizzes *hint hint*. Lecture-wise id say he was a very fun and was very interactive encouraging students to participate. The only cons i have for this professor is that sometimes he would talk to fast and he takes a while to put in grades.

Prof. Ayala was soo good! The grades were weekly quizzes, a paper and the midterm/final which were super easy since he let you know what was on them. He's also super nice! Attendance didn't matter but going to class wasn't tedious or anything and he remembers who shows up! I 1000% recommend taking him especially if you want an easy semester

analysis.name: Ayten Bayram

review_highlights.comment: LOVED her class. She is a fantastic teacher. Discussion is usually intense but  well worth it and interesting especially if other class members participate. Absolutely love and adore Professor Bayram. She is an avid teacher who cares both about the students and the topics.  She is willing to give you feedback on you work which will help ensure a 100 on the final paper. Has been my experience both times I've had her class. Discussion is pertinent and movie analysis are fun and interesting.

Too much reading and not enough lecturing. Discussions in class are usually unrelated and too deep into something which does not really matter. I didn't enjoy her class.

analysis.name: Raad Azzawi

He is always there  to help  if student faces any problem related to subject course.

His lecture slides are very informative and he goes over examples with the class

Dr. Azzawi is the BEST professor in the Civil Engineering Department. The classes he teaches are very difficult, but he makes learning the material fun and easy. He ALWAYS stops to make sure we understand the material and will put the rest of lecture on hold if we need more clarity!

Easy Professor. Honestly, avoid him. Tests/homeworks are too easy. His classes will not prepare u for the engineering world or the FE. Next structures class I took (mechanics of materials), I didn't know more than half the material already cover in statics.

analysis.name: Barbara Shipman

This class legitimately changed my life. Analysis 1 and 2 can be a very difficult subject, but Dr. Shipman makes all of this so intuitive. Though attendance is very mandatory

She is very all over the place. Homework isn't due, you just go over some questions in class. Participation is a part of your grade. Doesn't give you a straight answer when you ask questions, she makes you work it out and will kind of guide you to the answer.

analysis.name: Patryk Babiracki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Interesting class.  If you want to learn, you have to take responsibility and learn it on your own. He guides the discussion and the class. Babiracki's style in teaching is what I believed truly prepared me for upper level discourse and writing essays. Though some may see him as vague and abstract, his style in doing just that encourages a level of independence expected of higher courses. Do not expect him to hold your hand; he will simply give you the tools and allow you to work.

There was two essays overall, an outline, a final assignment and there were 5 "pop" quizzes, but usually you knew what day they would be. Attend, take notes and READ!! Do not slack on the reading.

Dr. Babiracki is an amazing professor! He's super passionate about the subject he teaches, and it makes all the difference to help students understand the subject. You will read a lot during the course, but all of the readings are interesting. You will learn a lot. Will definitely take again.

Dr. Babiracki is one of the best professors I've ever had. Certainly not the easiest, but not as hard as I've seen others make him out to be. Definitely fantastic lectures, and he structures assignments in a way that thoroughly prepares you for future upper-level writing courses.

analysis.name: Christian-Andrew Bagby-Wright
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

analysis.name: Rachel Baldridge

Such an amazing professor who always was communicative with her student. When I did attend class her lectures were so interesting and hilarious. Good Online class feels like a real class but light work and can correct all assignment (except quizzes and test) to a 100.

analysis.name: Kevin Barlow

prof has open book homeworks for practice to help understand the material, & big curves on exams. ngl tho i had to self study because i was lost during her lectures & the ppt slides were confusing/unclear to me. textbook is not mandatory but i got it bc i wasnt understanding anything from the powerpoints.

5/5

analysis.name: Jayant Bhalerao

analysis.name: Dan Degges

Even failing tests, you can easily pass as long as you put the effort.

Towards the end of the sem attendance will be taken for the final few quizzes. Final project is making a 5-7 min YT video which isn't too bad. The lectures themselves are interesting.

For history, a lot of assignments but then they are easy to knock off if you manage to do the required readings and follow his instructions. Clear grader and def wants to see his students succeed. No exams, one final essay and a few discussion posts. Overall, a really well structured class.

Discussion posts are graded on if you are active on them multiple times throughout the week. He doesn't accept late work. If you are taking other classes at the same time, say goodbye to any free time.

He has no respect for his students and is rude.
Pathetic. Never shows up to class and is strict for no reason.

Easy A class. All assignments are easy and straightforward. Definitely show up or else you will fall behind. The only complaint I have is the attitude I get from the professor. Seems like he doesn't want to be there teaching to us. Apart from that easy A class.

analysis.name: Earl Crisp
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Seems easy at first (not much hw, etc.) but the tests include things that weren't mentioned in the review. 2 tests (including final). He doesn't post grades on BB and he doesn't let you know what grades you make on projects or even if he has received your hw's. No office hours either.  Won't respond to emails no matter how many times you email him.

Very bad professor.  Refused to give us our end of the year project grades.  Refused to tell us what our curve was.  Refused to respond to emails.  Refused to tell us what was expected on each paper and project until right before it was due (sometimes even day of).  Refused to tell us WHEN a project was due until a couple days before.

Took the wife and husband. Both the same kind of people. Loses homework assignments. Puts random grades in the grade book. Really frustrating professor. Didn't teach us anything. Wife subbed us for a portion of the semester bc he was always gone. didn't teach us anything either. Both useless people, getting paid for doing nothing!

analysis.name: Mary Kate Earnest
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: shes a really nice teacher and is pretty easy and really tries to make scheduling papers and assignments easier for you and the class. shes always gives positive feedback on your papers and will tell you the things you need to improve in a respectful and non- invasive way. go to class everyday at the end of the semester you get extra credit!

Ms. Earnest is awesome! Great teacher. Always helpful comments on papers, but never condescending. Not wishy washy, straight and to the point. Grade relies heavily on writing grades. The minimal reading is very important to do. Mostly writing grade. Always willing to help!
She was a really awesome teacher. Pretty easy, but still expected you to work hard. Makes essays and assignments easier on everyone. Very clear about everything. I highly recommend this teacher.
Very helpful Highly recommend this teacher. very quick on emails and if u had to would easily give u an extension on an essay

analysis.name: Earl Andresen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Andresen lectured but no use taking notes, that info isn't on the tests. You MUST come to class because one day you get a quiz, the other you do a case study. It's basically his way of doing attendance. His tests are ok, as long as you read the chapters. Cases are pretty easy, just write something that kind of makes sense and you get credit.

Good professor.  As long as you went to class and participated in the "case studies", you could get a good grade in participation. The tests were a little on the difficult side, mostly because the majority of the questions were T/F and I am not that good at T/F tests. Fun teacher though, great stories to tell!

Dr Andresen is a down to earth teacher, a nice guy who will answer your questions. you do have to read the textbook to pass the quizes. if you miss quizes he will let you make em up on final week. Andresen likes to see his students succeed and is good at giving advice. Thanks Adresen

Andresen is an awesome and straight forward professor. There are no test only quizzes and case studies each week. We did'nt even have a final exam this semester. As long as you ead each chapter for each quiz each week you will do fine. U must attend each class or you'll miss grades.
He's really cool kinda flirty, makes tasteless jokes but knows his PR. You can learn a lot form him and he teaches u the need to know, not useless BS. Great real world info here.

analysis.name: Dylan Parks
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Such an amazing professor! Definitely take him if you get the chance. His lectures are interesting and engaging. He explains the material very well. He is never boring. The exams match the lectures. He gives clear information about what will be on the exams. He offers extra credit and bonus quizzes that help your grade.

A + P is a fairly tough class, but he made sure that he went over everything that we needed to know for the tests. Gave us some clever ways to remember things and added his own experience and stories where appropriate. You will still have to study outside of class to do well, but often we'd get to leave early once he finished lecture.

Dr. Parks is one of my favorite professors at UTA. He goes in-depth on his lecture and makes sure you know what will be on exams. Lectures are usually not the whole lecture time and he is super understanding. 10/10 recommend him for microbiology. I will for sure remember him when I graduate.

Best professor I have ever had! Honestly its the course itself that is difficult, but Dr. Parks does an absolute amazing job at explaining everything. He makes it clear that what he has on his power points is what will be on the exam, he also provides the textbook. He gives so many opportunities for extra credit, but be sure to come to class? 10/10

Park's lectures are very fast-paced and information-heavy. The exams are difficult as there is so much content, however, he gives you so many opportunities for extra credit. If you study before each class and keep up with the workload you will be fine. This was one of the hardest classes I have taken for nursing so far.

analysis.name: Mark Eakin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Take my advice and take Dr. Eakin for BSTAT.  I had a hard time understanding statistics but he did a great job explaining it in a way that I could understand. Thanks for a great semester Dr. Eakin!

Oh man this class was awful. He has this dull monotone voice that lulls you to sleep and does everything on the projectors and goes so fast there's no possible way to keep up with him. Tests are hard, he talks like everyone has a working knowledge of SAS (which I had never used in my life). Group projects are there and they are horrendous.

Great guy, poor teacher. Talks quickly and mumbles, so hard to follow. Teaches as if you're a stat major, not bus major. Doesn't clearly convey assignment due dates. Lectures and hw focus on math, so you study math. Then test catches you off guard by focusing on trick questions about terminology or interpretation of results. Frustrating.

This is the worst class I've taken. It doesn't matter if you come to class or not. He forces you to buy the code although it's worth less than 5% of the grade. Also, his grading is very unfair, he gives partial credit for the wrong questions, but he compares with the other students. If your answer is unique then no partial credit!

They seem to use this class to cover both normal bus majors as well as ones going into academic, research or phds. So, it's taught as if everyone is the latter. Joe avg bus majors get overwhelmed and demoralized as they bomb the class trying to scrape by with a C, which can drop them from their major if it keeps them from maintaining GPA reqs. smh
